selected_evidence.requirement: Forward inventory logs from node2 to node1 and persist them under /var/log/inventory/node2.log
selected_evidence.summary: Both configurations validated; node2 established a TCP connection and the exact pre-restart inventory marker appeared in the required node1 file.
node1 boot ID changed from 17b362d1-c234-4169-bc4e-114d01fdf401 to 5d9468c3-7a68-4d3f-9376-7537a9503ade. The listener recovered, existing data remained, and a new inventory marker arrived afterward.

node2 boot ID changed from 29011044-5356-46eb-ba9c-1470170355a7 to 7c21ee57-2a69-4769-8f68-ed0f6241bd6b. rsyslog recovered, re-established TCP forwarding, and node1 stored a new post-restart marker alongside both earlier records.

commands.command:
set -eu; sudo tee /etc/rsyslog.d/30-inventory-forward.conf >/dev/null <<'ANTRIEB_EOF'
if ($programname == "inventory") then {
  action(
    type="omfwd"
    target="10.100.137.10"
    port="514"
    protocol="tcp"
    template="RSYSLOG_SyslogProtocol23Format"
    TCP_Framing="octet-counted"
    action.resumeRetryCount="-1"
    queue.type="LinkedList"
    queue.filename="inventory_forward"
    queue.saveOnShutdown="on"
    queue.maxDiskSpace="100m"
  )
}
ANTRIEB_EOF
sudo rsyslogd -N1; sudo systemctl restart rsyslog; systemctl is-active rsyslog; sudo sed -n '1,120p' /etc/rsyslog.d/30-inventory-forward.conf; ss -ntp | grep '10.100.137.10:514' || true
